newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Export Credit Insurance sees 14 pct growth.
newsitem.headline: HK's Export Credit Insurance sees 14 pct growth.

text.p: Hong Kong's Export Credit Insurance Corp (ECIC) said on Tuesday it predicts business growth of 14 percent in the 1996/97 financial year.
Total exports of goods and services were expected to exceed HK$20 billion in the financial year ended March 31, ECIC commissioner Timothy Yiu said in a statement.
ECIC said claims paid out would amount to approximately HK$71 million, 57 percent higher than in 1995/96.

Insolvency was predicted to account for 30 percent of the total value of claims paid. Default would account for some 63 percent of claims, or HK$44 million, a rise of 157 percent on the previous year.
